purpose: Source-visible database effect contract for the first signed worker integration; this is not a grant list, RLS policy, or deployment approval.

operation.scope: One source event and its source reading at the currently owner-verified location, per transaction.

transaction.connection: One non-autocommit PostgreSQL connection for context setup, scoped reads, effects, and event/notification intent writes.
transaction.event_publication: EventBus.publish(commit=False); the handler owns the final commit or rollback.
transaction.context: Migration 405 can sign this exact tenant/location/resource/action scope; no dispatcher currently establishes it.
transaction.retry: The source-reading/rule receipt suppresses duplicate database effects; notification and event delivery remain durable worker responsibilities.

effects.required_boundary: Read only the requested sensor_reading source event whose type, source table, source ID, payload location, and joined reading all agree with signed scope. Publish only the sensor_alert intent through a bounded function that verifies the signed location and alert row. Never expose claim, lease, retry, delivery-receipt, or dead-letter mutation to this operation.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 407 bounds source-event selection inside receipt reservation; migration 408 adds a SECURITY DEFINER publisher that derives the canonical sensor_alert payload and priority from the signed-location alert and matching alert_created receipt. It inserts a pending event, accepts only identical stable-ID retries, rejects collisions, and leaves queue state untouched. kokonut_worker_execution has function EXECUTE only and no direct platform_event access. The handler still uses EventBus directly until credential-isolated integration.

effects.required_boundary: Read only the event source row at the signed location; event ID, event type, source table, sensor ID, and location must match.
effects.current_enforcement: Migrations 407 and 408 validate the event ID/type/table/source, payload location and every supplied sensor selector against the reading and device inside bounded functions. The handler remains unwired to signed worker context.

effects.required_boundary: Read enabled rules as shared read-only configuration. The event handler must not bootstrap, insert, update, or delete global alert rules.
effects.current_enforcement: Event processing skips default-rule bootstrap. Migration 407 requires an enabled rule for reservation; migration 408 derives alert event content from the matching alert/rule. Reads are confined to SECURITY DEFINER functions; there is no direct worker table grant.

effects.required_boundary: Read only sensor-type reference rows needed to interpret enabled alert rules.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 408 verifies the rule/device sensor-type relationship through its bounded event publisher; no direct worker table grant exists.

effects.required_boundary: Read the source device only when its ID and location match the signed scope and source reading.
effects.current_enforcement: Migrations 407 and 408 verify device identity and location against the source reading within bounded functions; no direct worker table grant exists and handler context is not integrated.

effects.required_boundary: Read the current authorized location's display name only; owner/tenant resolution remains in the signed context setter.
effects.current_enforcement: The event path constrains the device metadata join to the source location; it is not signed-context constrained.

effects.required_boundary: Cooldown reads must remain within the signed location and device. Inserts must match the source device, reading, and location. The only update is linking the newly created alert to its newly created draft claim.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 406 adds a nullable location_id and conservatively backfills matching device/reading pairs. Migration 408 reads only the alert linked by a matching alert_created receipt to derive the canonical event; no direct worker table grant exists. Existing handler cooldown reads/inserts remain application-scoped.

effects.required_boundary: Insert/update only the receipt for the signed source reading, source event, and rule. Preserve unique-key retry suppression; unresolved or cross-location source lineage must fail closed.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 406 adds a nullable location_id and conservatively backfills matching receipts. Migration 407 adds bounded reserve/outcome functions that validate signed location, event payload selectors, reading, device, rule, and alert linkage; the functions are not yet called by the handler and no worker login is provisioned.

effects.required_boundary: Create a claim only for the signed location and source reading, with status draft. The anomaly worker must not submit, verify, publish, reject, or otherwise transition lifecycle state.
effects.current_enforcement: Existing insert explicitly sets draft and location from the sensor device; no worker-specific permission exists.

effects.required_boundary: Append an audit row for the signed location and source reading. The operation must not update or delete prior audit rows.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 406 adds a nullable location_id; anomaly log writes pass the verified device/source location. Unresolved history remains NULL, and no worker INSERT boundary exists.

effects.required_boundary: Enqueue an intent for the signed location and newly published sensor_alert event. Do not claim, edit, replay, dispose, or deliver notification rows or attempts.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 409 adds a SECURITY DEFINER enqueue function requiring signed location, a matching source receipt and published alert event, fixed primary destination, and channel-specific payload allowlists. It inserts only a pending location-bound intent; identical retries do not mutate delivery state. The handler still uses direct enqueue until credential-isolated integration reorders alert-event publication before notification enqueue. Delivery claims and attempts remain separate.

effects.required_boundary: Record only an intent at the signed location and linked alert. Preserve the existing approval-required state; the anomaly worker cannot approve, send, execute, or access MQTT transport.
effects.current_enforcement: Migration 410 adds a separate non-login function owner and create_sensor_alert_actuation_intent. The function validates signed location, the source reading event/receipt, the alert, and its sensor_alert event, then derives command fields from the enabled rule. Fifteen disposable PostgreSQL 16 checks pass. It creates one idempotent intent, preserves approval/transport state on retry, and gives kokonut_worker_execution function EXECUTE without direct actuation_log access. The handler still writes through its current helper, and no worker credential or dispatch integration exists.

implementation_constraints: Do not grant the shared kokonut_runtime role worker execution or worker authorization-table access.
Prefer bounded SECURITY DEFINER functions for shared event/notification intents and other writes that otherwise expose global queue state.
Migration 406 adds nullable direct location lineage and leaves unresolved history NULL; before worker authorization, enforce these keys and keep NULL rows inaccessible to this worker.
Do not enable application-table FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or roll migration changes onto the candidate as part of this source contract.
Worker credentials must be isolated by operation at deployment before any dispatcher integration.
